answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price, but memory_c4 shows benchmarking against market rates previously moved them on both price and payment terms at renewal—this is the only lever that cuts cost without switching supply mid-shortage. Memory_c6 shows a multi-year commitment can unlock volume pricing as an alternative concession if the incumbent still resists a spot price cut. The line is at 94% with no buffer and the contract expires in 14 days, so switching or adding a source introduces delivery risk I cannot absorb. Deferring leaves the assembly line exposed. Negotiating terms—payment terms, volume tiers, multi-year structure, or service scope in lieu of unit price—is the single action that presses on the 18% mandate while keeping deliveries uninterrupted.
